correctness.rationale: A polarity sends each absolute point to a tangent containing no other absolute point. An involution on each nonabsolute line forces intersection with absolute set parity q+1. For odd q the q+1 absolute points are an oval; its tangent classification gives A,E,I point sets and exact counts of distinct R-neighbors by type. For even q every line meets the q+1-point blocking set, forcing it to be a line; its pole and remaining points define A,C,N types and exact R-neighbor support. Nonneighbor support within I vanishes only at odd q=3, and within N only at even q=2. The two-symbol formulas for each unary type and phase separator are legal by variable rebinding, and a symmetric permanent two-pebble strategy matches equality, relation and type using positivity support, proving equivalence at all depths. Independent q=2,3,5,7 coordinatized graph construction reproduced the type/neighborhood support; arbitrary eligible planes follow from geometry, not finite tests.

evidence: General two-pebble EF theory supplies an equivalence test, and parity oval/line geometry is classical. Neither inspected source provides all four phase tables with q=2/q=3 anomalies.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A stronger general polarity association-scheme classification might imply the FO2 equivalence in another language, but the inspected generic methods require these geometry-specific neighbor-positivity checks.
